subject: tu:game/world/gauntworld
value:
MWCC GC 1.2.5 family. A TARGET-ONLY REGISTER COPY THAT MWCC COALESCED AWAY IS SOMETIMES SOURCE-REACHABLE, AND THE LEVER IS BLOCK SCOPE - NOT DECLARATION ORDER, NOT INITIALIZER PRESENCE, AND NOT SIMPLY WRITING A SECOND VARIABLE. THIS IS THE INVERSE POLARITY OF THE addrlo/home-copy FAMILY (the case where the TARGET has the extra copy and OUR build is count-short), the direction claim.law.DC_copy-form-class-is-directional-and-its-inverse-population-is-unserved.20260901.v1 names as unserved, and it now has one measured positive and one measured boundary.

TELL. Target: a value is produced (call return, or a load), used through register X, and copied `mr Y,X` / `addi Y,X,0` into a second long-lived register that is then live past a control-flow join. Our build: no copy at all, because the producing variable and the join-live variable were assigned the SAME register. Our stream is exactly one instruction short and the whole downstream branch-displacement column shifts by 4, which regnorm's artifact split correctly quarantines.

THE POSITIVE, measured on gauntworld fn_8005E90C at +0x240. Target `bl SetItem` / `mr r30,r24` / ...; ours `bl SetItem` / (no copy). The source had a FUNCTION-SCOPE `Item* child;` reused by both arms of a two-way if/else and copied into the function-scope, join-live `Item* result;`. In the first arm the sequence was straight-line (`child = NewItemPtr(); SetItem(child,...); result = child;`), so MWCC coalesced child into result's register r30 and the copy vanished; in the second arm a CFG join sat between the definition and the copy, so the copy survived there in BOTH streams. CURE: declare a BLOCK-SCOPED local inside the first arm and rewrite every in-arm use to it, leaving `result = <block local>;` as the copy. real 158 -> 143, insns O268 -> O269 of 270, opcode multiset 4t -> 3t, and the cluster disappeared from --ops entirely.

THE BOUNDARY, measured the same session on gauntworld fn_8005D730 at +0xb0, a structurally identical tell (`lwz r0,224(r28)` / `cmpwi r0,25` / `mr r29,r0` / `blt` against our `lwz r29,...` / `cmpwi r29,25` / `blt`). Writing a SAME-SCOPE second local - `s32 raw = *(s32*)&item->data[4]; s32 amount = raw;` with the guard testing `raw` and the later calls taking `amount` - is NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL: the object bytes do not change at all, because MWCC folds a plain same-scope scalar copy before codegen. The source text never reaches the allocator's decision point.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, therefore: the lever works when the two names genuinely differ in SCOPE AND LIVE-RANGE SHAPE - a block-local confined to one arm versus a variable live across the join - and does not work when both names sit in the same block with the same lifetime, however carefully the uses are split between them. Screen the shape before spending the probe: if you cannot point to a scope boundary and a control-flow join that separate the two names, expect NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL.

TWO NON-CURES MEASURED ON THE SAME SITES, both cheap and both dead: (a) swapping the declaration order of the two pointers (`Item* result; Item* child;`) is NEUTRAL - contrast claim.law.SP_initializer-presence-outranks-declaration-position-in-callee-saved-numbering.20260901.v1, which governs callee-saved NUMBERING and is simply not what is at stake when both streams already agree on the destination register; (b) splitting a declaration-with-initializer into a bare declaration plus an assignment is NEUTRAL.

SCOPE NOTE FOR THE COST SIDE: on fn_8005E90C the fix closed a structural cluster but LOST objdiff fuzzy (96.1407 -> 95.9815) while real, opcode multiset and instruction-count distance all improved - see claim.law.GW_all-three-cheap-predictors-can-improve-while-fuzzy-loses.20260901.v1. Expect to have to arbitrate rather than assume a clean win.
